8267.long: Dean was able to notch exactly 12 stops for the fourth game in a row and fifth time this season. The linebacker is out to a great start to his first campaign in Las Vegas, registering 80 total tackles (38 solo), including 1.5 sacks, while also adding an interception and three forced fumbles over eight contests so far.

7016.short: Chinn recorded 10 total tackles (four solo) and an interception during Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets.
7016.long: Chinn had quite a day in Week 8, finishing second on the team in takedowns while also jumping in front of a deep ball from Jets quarterback Geno Smith for the safety's first interception of the year. Chinn has now compiled 56 total tackles (38 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding two forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries and an interception over eight contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

7039.short: White was signed by the Raiders on Thursday, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
7039.long: White was released by the team Tuesday to make room for Carter Runyon (foot), who was activated off injured reserve. With Runyon now waived and potentially joining the Raiders' practice squad, White was re-signed. To date, the 27-year-old has had the best season of his career, amassing eight catches (19 targets) for 112 yards and three touchdowns.

12670.short: Lambert-Smith registered one catch (on four targets) for 50 yards in Sunday's loss to Houston.
12670.long: Lambert-Smith wasn't exactly prolific in spite of logging a hearty 40 offensive snaps, but he made his one catch count, hauling in a 50-yard reception in the third quarter. However, the woeful Chargers turned the ball over on a fumble two plays later. Lambert-Smith has spent much of the season on IR and has had an inconsistent role when suiting up, but he was deployed pretty heavily Sunday because Ladd McConkey couldn't play due to back spasms. If McConkey is also sidelined next Monday in Baltimore, Lambert-Smith could again be a fairly big part of Los Angeles' air attack.

11647.short: Vidal rushed seven times for 30 yards in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. He added one catch for six yards on three targets.
11647.long: The Chargers continue to use a three-man backfield, an unfriendly fantasy situation and one to avoid when making lineup decisions each week. Vidal has been productive when he does get touches, rushing 36 times for 162 yards (4.5 YPC) and one touchdown across eight games. He's also caught 10 passes for 56 yards and an additional score.

12493.short: Gadsden caught two of three targets for 17 yards during the Chargers' 44-22 loss to the Texans on Sunday.
12493.long: Gadsden was on the field for 33 of 72 offensive snaps (45.8 percent), which was second-most among Chargers tight ends behind Charlie Kolar (47). Gadsden has caught two passes or fewer in six of eight regular-season games, and his 19-172-1 receiving line (on 29 targets) is well behind pace from his rookie campaign (49 catches on 69 targets for 664 yards and three scores across 15 regular-season contests). The Chargers' offense this season has struggled under quarterback Justin Herbert and coordinator Mike McDaniel, which doesn't bring much confidence ahead of their Week 10 road tilt against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.

8127.short: Kolar brought in all three of his targets for 31 yards in a 44-22 loss to the Texans on Sunday.
8127.long: Kolar has recorded three catches in four of his last five outings, although he's cracked 30-plus receiving yards in just two of those contests. The Chargers average a season-low 15.1 points per game, and their 201.9 receiving yards per game is ninth-fewest in the NFL, making pass catchers like Kolar hard to rely on for sustained production. The 0-8 Chargers will look to capture their first win of the season in Week 10 against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.

6797.short: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said that Herbert "should be good to go" for Monday's game at Baltimore after imaging on the quarterback's injured left middle finger returned negative for a fracture, ESPN.com reports.
6797.long: Herbert may still have to manage some discomfort in the finger during Monday's contest, but since the injury to his non-throwing hand, he shouldn't be too affected while throwing or handing the ball off. That being said, Herbert has become increasingly difficult to justify including in fantasy lineups even when he's been in more optimal health entering games. Heading into the matchup with the Ravens, Herbert has completed a career-low 61.3 percent of his passes for 6.8 yards per attempt and just six touchdowns in eight games. He's tied with New England's Drake Maye for the league lead in interceptions thrown (11) and ranks second behind Cleveland's Deshaun Watson in sacks taken (31).

12509.short: Harris caught three of seven targets for six yards during Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans.
12509.long: Harris failed to take advantage of Ladd McConkey (back) failing to appear in Sunday's game, registering his fewest receiving yards in a game this season. Harris was able to garner a team-high seven targets, which bodes well for his chances of increased production in Week 10 against the Ravens if McConkey remains sidelined.

11635.short: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh noted Monday that McConkey is viewed as "day to day" with back spasms, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
11635.long: McConkey was not among the Chargers' Week 9 inactives, but he didn't play any snaps in Sunday's loss to the Texans after experiencing back spasms during pregame workouts. Harbaugh's assessment that the wideout is 'day-to-day' offers hope that McConkey will be in the clear ahead of next Monday's game against the Ravens, and a big step toward that outcome would be his full participation in practice no later than Saturday.

8259.short: Dicker went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 44-22 loss to Houston.
8259.long: Dicker was able to make multiple field-goal tries for the third straight game and fifth time this season. The kicker did all his damage in the first half, converting field goals from 52, 33 and 43 yards before the break. Dicker has now gone 15-for-17 on field-goal attempts, including 1-for-2 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

12773.short: Uiagalelei completed two of seven passes for 27 yards and a touchdown after replacing Justin Herbert (finger) in the fourth quarter of Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans, and head coach Jim Harbaugh said after the game that Herbert could have a fractured finger, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
12773.long: Uiagalelei was inaccurate in his first taste of regular-season NFL action but threw a 15-yard touchdown pass to Derius Davis. If Herbert isn't available to face the Ravens on MNF in Week 10 and Trey Lance (groin) isn't ready to return from injured reserve, Uiagalelei would presumably be tabbed for the first regular-season start of the latter's career.

9754.short: Johnston caught one of four targets for a 58-yard touchdown in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans.
9754.long: Johnston's long touchdown catch cut the deficit to 38-15 in the fourth quarter. That was the final pass Justin Herbert (finger) completed before exiting the game. If Herbert can't play against the Ravens in Week 10, Johnston would likely find himself catching passes from DJ Uiagalelei. Johnston's 58 receiving yards set a new season high, surpassing his one-catch, 57-yard effort in Week 6, and Sunday's TD was his first of the season.

9511.short: Mitchell rushed seven times for 33 yards and caught three of four targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. He also lost a fumble.
9511.long: Mitchell led LA's three-man backfield rotation with 67 scrimmage yards, while Omarion Hampton had 60 and Kimani Vidal contributed 36. Mitchell's fumble came late in the third quarter, with the Chargers already trailing 31-9 at the time. The winless Chargers are averaging a league-low 15.1 points per game heading into a Week 10 trip to Baltimore, and things could get even worse if QB Justin Herbert (finger) has to miss time after getting injured in the fourth quarter.

12507.short: Hampton rushed 13 times for 60 yards and wasn't targeted in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans.
12507.long: Hampton worked as the Chargers' primary rushing option ahead of Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal, who recorded seven carries apiece. The 0-8 Chargers unsurprisingly faced another negative game script, though, and Hampton wasn't involved in the passing game. The 2025 first-round pick continues to disappoint on a surprisingly awful offense that could get even worse should QB Justin Herbert (finger) miss any additional action after exiting in the fourth quarter. Hampton will try to snap a four-game touchdown drought in Week 10 against the Ravens.

10234.short: Davis caught one of two targets for a 15-yard touchdown in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans.
10234.long: With Justin Herbert (finger) out of the game and the score out of hand already, Davis caught a 15-yard touchdown from backup DJ Uiagalelei in the fourth quarter. Davis has no fantasy value as a reserve wideout in one of the league's worst offenses.

11749.short: Hart (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Texans.
11749.long: Hart exited the third quarter of Sunday's game with an ankle injury. Rodney Shelley will play outside cornerback opposite Donte Jackson while Hart undergoes further evaluation.

13131.short: Waxter (ankle) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Texans.
13131.long: The special-teamer will not return to Sunday's contest after exiting in the first quarter. A number of players could step up to contribute on special teams in Waxter's absence.

11743.short: Eboigbe is questionable to return to Sunday's game against Houston due to an ankle injury, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
11743.long: Eboigbe was hurt in the first quarter, and his return is uncertain. Nick Barrett will likely pick up more defensive snaps for as long as Eboigbe remains sidelined.

2353.short: Perryman (undisclosed) was not activated ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans, per the NFL's transaction log.
2353.long: Perryman logged a pair of limited sessions during Week 9 prep but is not quite ready to return to the Chargers' 53-man roster. The inside linebacker will continue his recovery during Week 10 prep in the hopes of making his 2026 regular-season debut soon.

4033.short: Njoku (fibula) wasn't activated from IR-designated to return ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans, per the NFL's official transaction log.
4033.long: Njoku returned to practice this week but was limited all three days before being deemed doubtful for Week 9 action. The TE's next chance to play will arrive Monday, Nov. 16, when the Chargers face the Ravens.

13633.short: Shelley (ankle) has no designation for Sunday's tilt against the Texans.
13633.long: Shelley missed each of Los Angeles' past three games while tending to an ankle injury. However, he followed two limited practices to begin this week with a full session Friday to position himself for a return Sunday. Shelley has played a rotational role in the secondary when active this season while also contributing on special teams.

5051.short: Jackson (hamstring) does not have a designation for Sunday's tilt against the Texans.
5051.long: Jackson missed each of the Chargers' past three games due to a hamstring injury, but he was able to log a full practice session Friday and is set to return to action versus Houston. Before getting hurt, he started in three of his four appearances to begin the season, so he'll likely return to that role Sunday, especially since fellow cornerback Deane Leonard (concussion) has been ruled out.

3271.short: Higbee caught one of five targets for 13 yards during Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.
3271.long: Higbee was held to just one catch for a second consecutive game, although his 13-yard grab set the Rams up on the Commanders' one yard line and led to a rushing touchdown by Blake Corum on the next play. Higbee has only four catches over his last three games, but he figures to play a larger role in the passing game for at least the next month while Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is on injured reserve. The Rams will hit the road for Week 10 against the Cardinals, whose defense has given up six touchdowns to opposing tight ends this season, which ranks 25th in the NFL.

7562.short: Atwell recorded two catches on five targets for 16 yards during the Rams' 20-13 win over the Commanders on Sunday.
7562.long: Atwell ended up finishing second among Rams wide receivers in both targets and offensive snaps behind Puka Nacua. However, the Rams' offense will have to undergo a sizable overhaul in the absence of Nacua, who suffered a sprained PCL/MCL in his knee as well as turf toe during Sunday's win, with the superstar wide receiver expected to be sidelined for at least a month while on injured reserve, per Sarah Bishop of ESPN.com. Davante Adams (hamstring) is also on injured reserve, so that leaves Atwell and Konata Mumpfield as the top healthy wide receivers on the Rams' 53-man roster, and rookie sixth-rounder CJ Daniels is also in position for a larger role on offense. The Rams will face the Cardinals in Week 10, and Arizona's defense has given up 19 passing touchdowns on the year, which is second-most in the league behind Las Vegas' 20.

12718.short: Mumpfield caught both of his targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.
12718.long: Despite the lack of production, Mumpfield's 20 receiving yards ended up being second-most on the Rams behind Puka Nacua (150). The bigger news from Sunday's game was Nacua sustaining a PCL/MCL sprain in his knee and turf toe, and the superstar wide receiver is expected to miss at least one month while on injured reserve, per Sarah Bishop of ESPN.com. With Davante Adams (hamstring) also on IR until at least Week 11, that leaves the Rams with Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and rookie sixth-rounder CJ Daniels as the top wide receivers for Matthew Stafford. The Rams hit the road for Week 10 against the Cardinals, whose defense has given up 19 passing touchdowns, which is second-most in the NFL behind the Raiders (20).

11623.short: Whittington (back) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday.
11623.long: This is another blow to the Rams' receiving corps, as Davante Adams (hamstring) is still on IR and Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is slated to miss several weeks. Whittington would have had a chance to carve out a major role in Los Angeles' wideout room, but instead he'll be sidelined until at least Dec. 20. The Rams signed Xavier Smith off San Francisco's practice squad Tuesday to take Whittington's place on the 53-man roster and in the WR corps.

11168.short: The Rams signed Smith off the 49ers' practice squad Tuesday.
11168.long: Smith had been with the Rams early in the campaign before being waived Oct. 2. He subsequently signed with San Francisco's practice squad, where he had resided until Los Angeles brought him back into the fold Tuesday. Smith drew just one target (which he didn't catch) across 80 offensive snaps over his three games with the Rams in the early portion of the season, but he could immediately factor into the mix for the next several weeks, as Davante Adams (hamstring) is still on IR, Puka Nacua (knee) is slated to miss several weeks and Jordan Whittington (back) landed on injured reserve Tuesday. Smith could also be used as a returner in Whittington's absence.

12487.short: Rams head coach Sean McVay acknowledged Monday during his appearance on the "Coach McVay Show" that he remains hopeful Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) will return from injured reserve this season, though he was unwilling to guarantee that the tight end will be activated by the time his 21-day evaluation window closes, Cameron DaSilva of USA Today reports. "I'm reluctant to get too far ahead of anything, just because -- but yes, that is something we'd want to avoid if he's not prepared," McVay said, regarding the possibility of Ferguson being shut down.
12487.long: After missing five consecutive games while recovering from an ankle sprain, Ferguson appeared poised to return from IR ahead of this past Sunday's game against the Commanders, but his activation was delayed after he pulled his hamstring while running a route during Friday's practice. McVay said after the practice that the setback would likely keep Ferguson out for "a couple more weeks." Ferguson's 21-day window will come to a close Nov. 25, so even if he doesn't resume practicing before then, he'll likely need to show the Rams that he's made at least some progress in his recovery from the hamstring injury to get activated. McVay said that he would be open to adding Ferguson back to the 53-man roster before he's ready to play, but the Rams may not be keen on essentially playing a man down for more than a game or two.

6865.short: Parkinson notched four catches for 13 yards on four targets in a 20-13 win over Washington on Sunday.
6865.long: Parkinson ranked second on Los Angeles in receptions, though he didn't turn them into many yards. Still, it was his third straight contest with at least four catches, so Parkinson looks to be developing into a favorite target of QB Matthew Stafford. That could come in handy in Week 10 and beyond, as Stafford is going to need to turn to other pass catchers to help make up for the massive production being lost in the absence of Puka Nacua, who is expected to land on IR due to knee and turf-toe injuries.

1433.short: McManus made both of his field-goal tries and both PATs in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.
1433.long: McManus' field goals were good from 33 and 20 yards, and he's now made all 13 of his kicks through three games with Los Angeles. With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) now out for the foreseeable future, this offense figures to struggle to score points, downgrading McManus in the fantasy kicker rankings.

3973.short: Garrett recorded 3.0 sacks and forced a fumble in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.
3973.long: Making his return from a knee injury that had sidelined him since Week 1, Garrett made an immediate impact and accounted for three of the Rams' four sacks of Jayden Daniels on the afternoon, with Braden Fiske and Shaun Dolac splitting the other. A healthy Garrett's presence in the front seven changes the entire complexion of the defense, and he could continue to make up for lost time in Week 10 against Gardner Minshew and the Cardinals.

11586.short: Corum carried the ball 11 times for 58 yards and a touchdown and failed to catch either of his two targets in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.
11586.long: The Rams' backfield has become a full-fledged timeshare, with Corum getting double-digit carries for a third straight game and out-producing Kyren Williams on the ground in Washington. Corum has gotten into the end zone in all three of those contests, punching in a one-yard score in the third quarter Sunday, and over that stretch he's amassed 224 rushing yards and three TDs while averaging 5.7 yards a carry. With Puka Nacua (knee) headed for an MRI, the Rams could lean even more heavily on their ground attack in a Week 10 tilt against the Cardinals.

421.short: Stafford completed 26 of 43 passes for 228 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders. He added one yard on his only carry.
421.long: The veteran QB looked the way of Puka Nacua (knee) early and often, with no other Ram pass catcher managing more than 20 receiving yards, and the star wideout was on the other end of a seven-yard TD toss in the fourth quarter that proved to be the winning score. Stafford has thrown a single touchdown pass in back-to-back games after producing multiple TDs in five of six contests before that, and his options could get even thinner with Nacua headed for an MRI after getting hurt on L.A.'s final possession.

8150.short: Williams carried the ball 15 times for 45 yards and caught three of four targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 20-13 win over Washington.
8150.long: Blake Corum was the more productive Ram on the ground, turning 11 carries into 58 yards and a touchdown, but the offense mainly flowed through Puka Nacua on the afternoon. Williams failed to find the end zone for only the third time in nine games this season, and the 45 rushing yards were his lowest total since Week 1, although he has yet to reach 100 in any contest. The Los Angeles backfield has become a clear timeshare however, limiting Williams' upside heading into a Week 10 trip to Arizona.

7750.short: Stuard is listed as active for Sunday's matchup against the Commanders.
7750.long: Stuard finished the week as a limited participant in Friday's practice due to a hamstring injury that occurred during Week 8 warmups. The 28-year-old has played in all eight Rams games this season, recording two total tackles (one solo).

7136.short: Curl (foot) is active for Sunday's game against the Commanders.
7136.long: Curl is set to suit up for Sunday's game despite missing the Rams' Wednesday and Thursday practice sessions. The strong safety will need to anchor the team's secondary due to the absence of starting cornerbacks Jaylen Watson (shoulder, IR) and Trent McDuffie (back).

8373.short: The Rams placed Watson (shoulder) on injured reserve Saturday.
8373.long: Watson exited Sunday's win over the Chargers early with a severe shoulder injury. The cornerback will undergo surgery while on IR, which will end his season. Watson ends the season with 24 tackles (14 solo) and nine passes defensed, including one interception, over seven regular-season games.

8195.short: The Rams activated Rivers (calf) from injured reserve Saturday.
8195.long: Rivers missed six games while on injured reserve with a calf injury he sustained in the Rams' Week 2 loss to the Giants. The 27-year-old has returned ahead of Sunday's game against the Commanders and has no injury designation headed into the contest. Rivers will likely be a special-teams contributor with no real role in the Rams' offense.

8161.short: The Dolphins hope Willis (abdomen) will return this year but haven't ruled out season-ending surgery, Joe Schad of The Palm Beach Post reports.
8161.long: With that in mind, coach Jeff Hafley noted that Willis had an MRI to assess his core muscle injury, and will continue to explore medical opinions. The team already placed Willis on injured reserve, ruling him out through Week 13. The latest report suggests that it's still unclear whether Willis will miss four games, the rest of the season or something in between. Kyle McCord is taking over at QB for the Dolphins in the meantime, with Hafley on Wednesday noting of Willis' job security in general, "he'll be the starting quarterback if he returns."

13338.short: Coleman wasn't targeted in Sunday's 19-9 loss to the Lions. He rushed one time for 16 yards.
13338.long: Coleman logged just 11 offensive snaps, and he's settled back in as the Dolphins' fourth receiver with all three of Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell healthy ahead of him on the depth chart. Coleman, a fifth-round rookie out of Missouri has no fantasy appeal.

13311.short: Bell failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 19-9 loss to the Lions.
13311.long: The Dolphins completed just 14 passes against Detroit, and Bell had his fourth zero-catch game of the season. With Caleb Douglas and Malik Washington healthy, Bell is the WR3 in an offense that can barely even support one pass catcher in the box score most weeks. Bell has 12 grabs for 148 yards and no touchdowns on 27 targets through eight games.

5297.short: The Dolphins placed Sieler (biceps) on injured reserve Tuesday.
5297.long: This move was anticipated after Sieler suffered a ruptured biceps in Sunday's Week 9 loss to the Lions. The veteran defensive tackle is scheduled for surgery and will finish his ninth NFL campaign with 24 tackles, including 2.0 sacks. Zeek Biggers, Kenneth Grant and Jordan Phillips could all take on more defensive snaps with Sieler sidelined for the rest of the season.

12494.short: McCord will step in as the Dolphins' starting quarterback beginning with Sunday's game at Indianapolis after Miami placed Malik Willis (core) on injured reserve Tuesday, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports.
12494.long: A 2025 sixth-round pick of the Eagles, McCord will be making his NFL debut Sunday, after he had been active for each of the 1-7 Dolphins' first eight games but didn't see any playing time behind Willis. Before landing with the Dolphins in a trade prior to Week 1, the 24-year-old signal-caller looked sharp during preseason action as a member of the Packers, completing 46 of 70 passes for 446 yards and a 4:0 TD:INT while adding 16 yards on five carries over three games. Expectations should still be held in check for McCord in his first regular-season action, especially while he'll be working with one of the NFL's weaker collections of skill-position players. The Dolphins are optimistic that Willis will be able to return from IR before the end of the season, but McCord should be primed for at least a four-game run as the team's starter while Willis is sidelined.

4233.short: Gonzalez reverted to the Dolphins' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
4233.long: Miami now has used the maximum three standard elevations on Gonzalez, and he's made just five of seven field-goal attempts and all five PATs across three games. The Dolphins will need to sign the kicker to the active roster if he's going to keep kicking for the team moving forward.

13405.short: Allen caught a 46-yard pass in Sunday's 19-9 loss to the Lions. He rushed one time for minus-1 yard.
13405.long: Allen's catch came on a fake punt, so it was an outlier of a play. He played just six offensive snaps behind clear RB1 Ollie Gordon. Since joining Miami via waivers last month, Allen has logged 31 snaps on special teams and six on offense. He has no fantasy appeal.

8172.short: Dulcich caught two of four targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 19-9 loss to the Lions.
8172.long: Entering play Sunday, Dulcich produced 13 grabs for 166 yards over his previous three games, but he took a big step back against Detroit on a day Malik Willis didn't have any answers, as he passed for just 128 yards. Dulcich doesn't catch touchdowns and plays in a low-volume, low-scoring offense, making him more of a TE2 headed into Week 10 against the Colts.

11610.short: Washington caught two of three targets for 21 yards during Sunday's 19-9 loss to the Lions.
11610.long: Washington was held in check by Detroit's suspect secondary, failing to reel in at least three passes for the first time this season. In addition, his 21 receiving yards were also a season low. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 70 receiving yards in a game this year, and he has reached the end zone only once. Washington will have an opportunity to get back on track against the sputtering Colts in Week 10.

13296.short: Douglas secured six of eight targets for 70 yards in the Dolphins' 19-9 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
13296.long: Douglas led the Dolphins in receptions, receiving yards and targets, as the rookie third-round pick continued to profile as one of Malik Willis' most reliable targets. Douglas' catch and target totals were also new career highs, while his yardage tally tied for the second highest of his nascent NFL tenure. Douglas should continue to play a key role in Miami's air attack over the second half of the season as the Dolphins look to continue cultivating their young talent.

12495.short: Gordon rushed 16 times for 55 yards and brought in his only target for nine yards in the Dolphins' 19-9 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
12495.long: Gordon worked in the lead role as expected but found running room at a premium against a game Lions defense. Gordon has at least Sunday's carry total in four straight games, but he's now seen his rushing yardage total decline in consecutive games. Jaylen Wright's inactive status due to a quadriceps injury helped Gordon's touch floor overall, and the latter should remain the top option in Miami's ground attack in a favorable Week 10 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

13434.short: Kacmarek is dealing with a quad injury and is questionable to return to Sunday's clash against Detroit.
13434.long: Kacmarek took a low hit after making a catch in the third quarter and subsequently went to the medical tent. He then returned to the sideline and tested out the injured leg, so he appears to be at least attempting to re-enter the contest. If Kacmarek can't return, however, Greg Dulcich and Seydou Traore will be Miami's two healthy active tight ends.

8001.short: Herring (neck) is active for Sunday's game against the Lions.
8001.long: Herring suffered a neck injury in the Week 8 loss to New England. Despite logging three limited practices throughout the week and being listed as questionable, he's good to go for the meeting with Detroit. The 28-year-old has appeared in seven regular-season games in 2026, accruing nine total tackles (four solo) and 1.0 sacks.

13453.short: Rodriguez notched eight tackles (two solo) and forced a fumble in Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots.
13453.long: Rodriguez fell three tackles shy of Jordyn Brooks' team-leading total as the Dolphins dropped to 1-6. The rookie second-round pick's 12 tackles over the past two games mark the most fallow two-game stretch of Rodriguez's young career in that category. He'll try to pick up the pace in Week 9 against the Lions.

1166.short: Head coach Kevin O'Connell said Wednesday that he isn't ready to commit to Cousins as the Vikings' Week 10 starting quarterback, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
1166.long: Minnesota acquired Cousins via trade from Las Vegas on Tuesday, but even though he has experience working under O'Connell from his previous stint with the team in 2022 and 2023, the coach will wait to make a decision. It appears Kyler Murray is set to miss another game Sunday at Green Bay, meaning Cousins, Carson Wentz (ankle) and Max Brosmer are the options to get the call this weekend.

6794.short: Jefferson stands to benefit from Tuesday's acquisition of Kirk Cousins, who is expected to take over as the Vikings' starting quarterback beginning with Sunday's game against the Packers, Michael F. Florio of ESPN.com reports.
6794.long: Jefferson had averaged a career-low 56.1 receiving yards per game through the first eight contests while the Vikings had the likes of Kyler Murray (hamstring), Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer under center, but the star receiver looks to be one of the biggest winners in the aftermath of the deadline. He'll be reunited with Cousins, who was at the helm for Jefferson's first four years in the league, when the wideout averaged 98.0 yards per contest and had a 17-game pace of 1,671 and 8.5 touchdowns. Though Cousins is three years older from when he last donned a Vikings uniform, he enjoyed a resurgent start to the season in Las Vegas, ranking second in the NFL in passing touchdowns (20) and fifth in passing yards (2,340) despite playing behind a weak offensive line and working with an underwhelming receiver group. Cousins' hot start and history with Jefferson should give Jefferson's fantasy managers added confidence in his rest-of-season outlook.

12496.short: Felton went without a target while playing six of the Vikings' 48 offensive snaps in Monday's 23-6 loss to the Bills.
12496.long: Felton continues to handle a muted role as a depth receiver for Minnesota, as Monday marked the third consecutive game in which he played single-digit snaps. For the season, the second-year wideout out of Maryland has been limited to just three receptions for 41 yards on seven targets over eight appearances.

6931.short: Dallas caught his only target for a two-yard gain in Monday's Week 9 loss to the Bills.
6931.long: Dallas notched just eight offensive snaps but also contributed 19 snaps on special teams. The veteran running back went without a carry for the fourth time over Minnesota's past five games, indicating his lack of a role in the running game. Overall this season, Dallas has been a very small part of the Vikings' offense, recording four carries for 14 yards and five catches for 36 yards (on five targets) through eight contests.

13075.short: Price caught one of his four targets for six yards in a Week 9 loss to Buffalo on Monday Night Football. He also gained 12 yards on one punt return and brought back four kickoffs for 124 yards.
13075.long: Price wasn't the only Minnesota pass catcher who logged an inefficient line, as starting quarterback Carson Wentz completed just eight of 25 pass attempts. Price did make an impact in the return game by averaging 31.0 yards on his four kickoff returns. Price's role continues to be mostly centered on special teams, as he's caught just four passes for 32 yards on 11 targets through eight games.

11792.short: Reichard made both of his field-goal attempts during the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday.
11792.long: After missing his lone field-goal attempt in Week 8 against the Lions, Reichard bounced back Monday to connect on field goals from 43 and 53 yards in the second quarter, which ended up being the only points that the Vikings scored. Reichard's 20 made field goals through eight regular-season games is tied for fourth-most in the NFL, and his seven makes from 50-plus yards is tied with Ka'imi Fairbairn for second behind Spencer Shrader (eight). The Vikings are 6-2 despite their struggles on offense this season, but the acquisition of Kirk Cousins should help make the unit more efficient. Minnesota will travel to Lambeau Field for Week 10 against Green Bay on Nov. 15.

12775.short: Brosmer completed six of seven attempts for 58 yards in Monday night's 23-6 loss to the Bills.
12775.long: Brosmer replaced Carson Wentz in the fourth quarter of Monday night's game after the offense failed to produce a touchdown drive. Week 9 was Brosmer's first appearance in a 2026 regular-season game. He will likely play a similar backup role behind newly acquired Kirk Cousins as the season progresses, at least until Kyler Murray returns from a hamstring injury.

2078.short: The Vikings released Beckham on Tuesday, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.
2078.long: Signed off the practice squad ahead of Monday's game against the Bills, Beckham made his Vikings debut in the 23-6 loss, going without a target while playing just two snaps on offense. He'll end up giving up his spot on the 53-man roster just one day later after the Vikings brought in quarterback Kirk Cousins in a trade with the Raiders prior to the deadline, but Beckham won't be without a home for long. Per Tom Pelissero of Netflix, Beckham is expected to re-sign with the Vikings' practice squad and will be eligible to be elevated for three more games.

9756.short: Addison secured two of three targets for 28 yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night.
9756.long: Addison finished third in receptions and receiving yards on the night for a low-volume Vikings passing game, and his final catch, which went for 16 yards, came on Minnesota's last drive from the arm of Max Brosmer. Carson Wentz's game-long ineffectiveness depressed the production of the air attack as a whole, but Addison would be in better position to boost his numbers if Kyler Murray (hamstring) is able to return for Sunday's Week 10 road matchup against the Packers.

4199.short: Jones rushed five times for 16 yards and brought in his only target for five yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night.
4199.long: Jones and backfield mate Jordan Mason combined for just 11 carries on an abysmal night for the Vikings offense, and the latter was much more efficient than Jones by averaging 5.8 yards per carry on his six totes. Jones now has seen his rushing yardage totals drop in three straight games, and Mason's return from injured reserve has played a role in the former seeing just 18 total carries in the last three contests. Jones retains a very modest outlook for a Week 10 road matchup against his old Packers teammates Sunday.

8408.short: Mason rushed six times for 35 yards and brought in two of three targets for seven yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night.
8408.long: Mason was markedly more efficient than backfield mate Aaron Jones with his opportunities, averaging 5.8 yards per carry compared to the latter's 3.2. Both backs' touches were limited due to game script, however, but Mason's YPC was an encouraging figure. The veteran back next takes aim at the Packers defense in a Week 10 road matchup on Sunday.

5844.short: Hockenson recorded four catches for 33 yards on seven targets in a loss to Buffalo on Monday.
5844.long: In addition to leading the Vikings in receptions, Hockenson finished second in receiving yardage and targets in a rough performance by Minnesota's offense. The veteran wideout has hauled in exactly four catches in four straight games, though he snapped a two-game TD streak Monday. It remains to be seen who will be throwing passes for Minnesota next Sunday in Green Bay, as Carson Wentz struggled enormously Monday and Kyler Murray currently is dealing with a Grade 2 hamstring strain.

12683.short: Ingram-Dawkins exited Monday night's game against the Bills with an ankle injury and is questionable to return.
12683.long: Levi Drake Rodriguez, Elijah Williams and Jalen Redmond will handle more of the defensive-line duties with Ingram-Dawkins sidelined.

2130.short: Van Noy (calf) has returned to Monday night's matchup with Buffalo, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.
2130.long: Van Noy was briefly sidelined with a calf injury in the first quarter, but he has now returned to action. The 35-year-old will continue to operate in his primary reserve role at weak-side linebacker versus the Bills.

8496.short: Jackson (quadriceps) is active for Monday's game against Buffalo, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.
8496.long: Jackson did not practice Thursday and Friday. While he practiced in a limited capacity Saturday, it still wasn't enough to avoid a questionable designation. However, Jackson has since been upgraded and is ready to go versus the Bills.

6183.short: Van Ginkel (chest) doesn't have a designation for Monday's matchup against the Bills, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.
6183.long: Van Ginkel was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday but was able to upgrade to full participation Saturday. He's thus clear to suit up on Monday Night Football against the Bills. That's a big deal for the Vikings in their quest to slow down Josh Allen, as Van Ginkel leads the team with 6.5 sacks through seven games.

12969.short: Larison recorded a four-yard rush and failed to haul in his lone target during the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday. He also recorded two tackles (one solo) on special teams.
12969.long: Both of Larison's tackles came while on kickoff coverage, and his lone touch on offense took place early in the fourth quarter. It was Larison has seen little activity in the Patriots' offense over the team's last two games, but that could change given that Rhamondre Stevenson is expected to be out for "the next few weeks" due to a knee injury he sustained Sudnay, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. TreVeyon Henderson (illness) doesn't have a clear timeline of return, so Larison and Corey Kiner are currently slated to be the Patriots' top backfield options for Week 10 against the Lions in Detroit.

12547.short: Williams failed to catch either of his two targets in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.
12547.long: With Mack Hollins (calf) back in the lineup, Williams still held a big snap share, playing 78 percent of the Patriots' offensive snaps against Green Bay. Efton Chism (51 percent) was the biggest loser in terms of playing time. Williams has earned just 15 targets across nine games this season, catching seven passes for 190 yards and two touchdowns.

13421.short: Raridon caught three passes for 52 yards on six targets in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.
13421.long: Even with Hunter Henry (foot) active, Raridon out-targeted the veteran six to three and produced 52 yards to Henry's 35 on the same amount of catches. Raridon has been a big-play threat as a rookie, averaging 14.1 yards per catch on 16 grabs this season, turning his 26 targets into 225 yards and two touchdowns. He's one of the better back-end TE2 options in fantasy.

12713.short: Borregales made all three of his PATs in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.
12713.long: Borregales didn't attempt a field goal, and it was the second time this season that he didn't kick any. For the year, the second-year kicker in 10 of 13 on FGAs and has made 23 of 24 extra points. He'll be a fantasy target for next Sunday's potential shootout in Detroit.

12491.short: Kiner rushed eight times for 55 yards and a touchdown and returned nine kickoffs for 224 yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday.
12491.long: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was inactive and Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) exited the game in the second half, a pair of developments that, when paired with the blowout nature of the contest, afforded Kiner some solid run. The Cincinnati product eclipsed the 50-yard mark on the ground for the third time this season, and he finished as the team leader in rushing yards. Kiner also recorded his first career touchdown on a four-yard run with just under four minutes remaining, and he'll be in line for an expanded role in Week 10 against the Lions in Germany if neither Stevenson nor Henderson are available.

9501.short: Douglas brought in five of nine targets for 102 yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday.
9501.long: Douglas tied for the team lead in receptions and set the pace in both receiving yards and targets while serving as Drake Maye's top target in the absence of A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder). Douglas also recorded a team-high 36-yard grab among his five catches, and both the yardage and target tallies were season highs. Douglas has at least 76 receiving yards in three of the past four games heading into a Week 10 matchup against the Lions in Germany next Sunday.

11564.short: Maye completed 21 of 38 passes for 299 yards with three touchdowns and three interceptions while adding one rush for three yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday.
11564.long: Maye was constantly harassed by an aggressive Packers defense that sacked him four times for 27 total yards in losses while also repeatedly getting hands on his throws. Working with a receiving corps that welcomed back Mack Hollins (calf) from injured reserve but was still down A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder), Maye threw his first interception on the second play of the game on a deep pass intended for Hollins, and his other two picks came during the second quarter. Two of the three INTs led to Green Bay touchdowns, and after throwing just eight interceptions over 17 regular-season games in 2025, Maye is up to 11 over nine contests this season following Sunday's game. The third-year signal-caller's first chance to atone comes in a Week 10 matchup against a seemingly improved Lions defense in Munich, Germany, next Sunday.

4177.short: Hollins caught three of six targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Patriots.
4177.long: After missing four weeks on injured reserve with a calf injury, Hollins returned to the lineup Sunday and immediately became a central part of the offense, tying Kyle Williams for second on the team with 34 routes on 46 dropbacks by New England's quarterbacks. Hollins' six targets also tied Eli Raridon for second on the team behind DeMario Douglas' nine. With A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder) still not 100 percent, Hollins figures to remain a big part of the picture next Sunday against the Lions in a potential shootout under the dome at Ford Field.

12542.short: Chism caught all five of his targets for 49 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.
12542.long: Chism was able to reel in exactly five passes for the second straight week, and he connected with quarterback Drake Maye for an eight-yard touchdown in the second quarter. The score was Chism's second of the year and first since Week 4. With A.J. Brown (knee) potentially set to miss the team's Week 10 matchup against the Lions, Chism may have a chance to operate in a prominent role again against Detroit's underwhelming secondary.

3214.short: Henry caught all three of his targets for 35 yards during Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.
3214.long: Henry returned to action after suffering a foot injury in the first half of the Patriots' Week 8 win over the Dolphins and missing the majority of that contest. The tight end was held in check versus Green Bay, finishing with three or fewer catches for the sixth time this season. Henry has now reeled in 32 of 37 targets for 361 yards and two touchdowns over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

8726.short: Schooler (hamstring) will not return to Sunday's game against the Packers.
8726.long: Strictly a special-teamer for New England, Schooler entered play Sunday with four tackles (two solo) across four games this season. His next chance to play will be next Sunday in Detroit.

5054.short: Davis (knee) is questionable to return to New England's matchup Sunday versus the Packers.
5054.long: Davis is in danger of missing the remainder of the game after suffering a knee injury in the second half. Channing Canada and Karon Prunty could be in line for an uptick in playing time if Davis is unable to return to the matchup.

13457.short: Jacas (knee) does not have a designation for Sunday's contest versus Green Bay.
13457.long: Jacas made an early exit last Sunday versus Miami due to a knee issue. He was limited in the first two Patriots practices this week but was able to upgrade to full participation Friday, clearing the way for him to suit up in Week 9.

13533.short: Brown caught his only target for 52 yards during Sunday's 23-22 overtime win versus the Browns. He also lost a fumble on a punt return.
13533.long: Brown showed off his plus speed in the second quarter, blowing by safety Ronnie Hickman and coming down with a 52-yard bomb from quarterback Tyler Shough. One series later, though, he coughed up the football during an erratic punt return. Barring an injury to one of the wideouts ahead of him on New Orleans' depth chart, there likely won't be much room in the short term for him to earn a significant role outside of special teams.

13420.short: Lance failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.
13420.long: With Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) making his regular-season NFL debut against Cleveland, Lance saw his snaps cut against Cleveland. After playing 79 percent of the offensive snaps in Week 7 against Pittsburgh, Lance logged just 51 percent of the plays versus the Browns. He has nine catches for 78 yards and a touchdown on 23 targets this season.

7543.short: Head coach Kellen Moore said Monday that the Saints haven't yet determined whether Etienne (hamstring) will return from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Panthers, Luke Johnson of The New Orleans Times-Picayune reports. "We'll see," Moore said. "He's progressing well. We'll gather some more information and make a decision."
7543.long: Moore noted that the Saints are still in the process of  "using the time allotted" to let Etienne work out with the training staff before designating him for return from injured reserve and opening his 21-day practice window. Though the 27-year-old back hasn't played since the Saints' Week 3 loss to the Raiders, he's still just 34 yards behind quarterback Tyler Shough for the team lead in rushing yardage (162). Whether he's activated for Week 10 or at some point thereafter, Etienne's eventual return will provide a boost to a New Orleans running game that has struggled mightily through the midway point of the season.

11653.short: The Saints reverted Smyth to their practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
11653.long: Smyth was elevated ahead of Sunday's Week 9 overtime win over Cleveland. He served as New Orleans' kicker in the contest and went 3-for-4 on FGAs while making both of his PAT attempts. That performance was likely good enough for Smyth to be elevated again for this Sunday's matchup against the Panthers.

5857.short: Fant caught one pass for 12 yards on two targets in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win against Cleveland.
5857.long: The veteran tight end logged 47 percent of the offensive snaps but is mainly a blocker, while Juwan Johnson handles most of the pass-catching duties at the position. Fant has four catches for 30 yards over his last four games and is not even remotely on the fantasy radar.

11834.short: Vele caught two passes for 17 yards on four targets in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.
11834.long: With Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) making his regular-season debut against Cleveland, Vele's role remained steady, running 44 routes on Tyler Slough's 46 dropbacks. Bryce Lance and Noah Fant appeared to be the bigger losers in terms of playing time and routes. Still, Tyson figures to have an effect on Vele's target potential moving forward, as he's setting in as more of a low-floor WR4/5 in fantasy.

4035.short: Kamara rushed six times for 32 yards while catching three of four targets for 17 yards during Sunday's 23-22 overtime win against the Browns.
4035.long: Kamara operated as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield behind Audric Estime (15-72-1) in Week 9. Estime was claimed off waivers from the Browns on Tuesday, and he immediately supplanted Kamara as the team's lead back. Kamara has yet to exceed 40 rushing yards in a game this season, and he has scored just one touchdown over the team's last four contests combined.

7002.short: Johnson caught both of his targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.
7002.long: Johnson made a catch early in the game but wasn't heard from again until overtime, when he caught a 15-yard touchdown to open the extra period. It proved to be the game-winner after the Browns failed on their two-point conversion following their touchdown with one minute left on the clock. After a strong start to the season in which he caught three touchdowns and posted 50-plus yards in each of the first four games, Johnson has been limited to just 57 yards and one score on seven grabs across the last four contests. With rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson back to muddy the picture even further, Johnson is more of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet.

13281.short: Tyson caught four of five targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns. He also lost a fumble.
13281.long: It wasn't the most dynamic performance from the eighth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, but it was just good to see Tyson on the field after he missed the first seven games of the season due to hamstring trouble, even if his longest gain went for just nine yards. Tyson's role in the offense figures to grow quickly if he can stay healthy, and he has the talent to put together a productive second half as the No. 2 option behind Chris Olave for quarterback Tyler Shough.

11579.short: Estime carried the ball 15 times for 72 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns. He also caught his only target for five yards.
11579.long: Claimed off waivers by New Orleans earlier in the week to add some depth to a depleted backfield, Estime ended up going up against his former Browns squad in his first game since rejoining the Saints. Since he had played for the Saints in 2025 and didn't need to learn head coach Kellen Moore's playbook, Estime was in prime position to step into a big role right away and capitalized on the opportunity, leading the backfield with 16 touches ahead of Alvin Kamara's nine. Estime capped his big performance with a two-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. While he certainly made a case for a consistent role in the offense, rookie CJ Donaldson (shoulder) could be back next week and Travis Etienne (hamstring) might be close to returning from injured reserve. Estime could still be atop the depth chart, at least temporarily, for a Week 10 clash with the Panthers.

12545.short: Shough completed 21 of 35 passes for 265 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.
12545.long: New Orleans got by with three Charlie Smyth field goals and an Audric Estime two-yard TD run in regulation, but Shough connected with Juwan Johnson for a 15-yard touchdown in OT that held up as the winning score when the Browns scored on the subsequent possession but failed on a two-point attempt -- the same way the Saints lost to the Lions in their season opener. Shough will take a 14:6 TD:INT through eight games into a Week 10 clash with the Panthers.

8144.short: Olave caught seven of 12 targets for 98 yards in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over Cleveland.
8144.long: The fifth-year wideout led the Saints in catches, targets and receiving yards once again, but Juwan Johnson was on the other end of Tyler Shough's only TD of the day. Olave is the clear top option in the New Orleans passing attack, but with Jordyn Tyson finally making his pro debut Sunday, secondaries may have someone else to worry about in the second half of the season. Olave will take a 56-734-2 line on 83 targets into a Week 10 battle against the Panthers.

8390.short: Emerson is listed as active for Sunday's matchup against the Browns.
8390.long: Emerson didn't participate in Friday's practice after kicking off the week limited Wednesday and Thursday. He appears to be ready to go, as he's not on the Saints' list of inactive players. The 26-year-old has 18 total tackles (16 solo), four pass deflections and two interceptions in six games.

5036.short: Reid (concussion) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns.
5036.long: Reid was a full participant in all three Week 9 practice sessions. The Saints' starting strong safety has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and is all set to suit up for Sunday's game against the Browns.

11597.short: Johnson wasn't targeted in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles.
11597.long: The tight end played just 12 offensive snaps, logging a 17.9 percent snap share against Philly. On the season, Johnson has just four catches for 55 yards and a touchdown on nine targets across six appearances. He has no fantasy appeal with Isaiah Likely healthy.

7090.short: Mooney (chest) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
7090.long: Listed as a limited participant for Monday's walk-through practice, Mooney took every rep a day later to erase any concern about his status heading into Thursday's game against the Commanders. The veteran wideout has played more than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in all but one of the Giants' eight games to date, but he exceeded two receptions and 50 receiving yards for the first time all season in this past Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. He remains a relatively unappealing fantasy option while receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely are locked in as the Giants' clear top two pass catchers.

11565.short: McCarthy (hip) was listed as a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
11565.long: McCarthy was sidelined for most of the third quarter of this past Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles after sustaining a painful hip pointer, but he was able to finish out the game. Head coach John Harbaugh expressed confidence afterward that the injury wouldn't be anything that jeopardized McCarthy's status for Thursday's game against the Commanders, and the quarterback's ability to take every rep Tuesday clears the way for him to start on a short week. Through two starts and two appearances off the bench with the Giants, McCarthy has completed 43 of 68 pass attempts (63.2 percent) for 622 yards (9.1 YPA), one touchdown and one interception to go with 51 yards on nine carries.

12481.short: Skattebo (hamstring) was listed as a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
12481.long: Prior to Tuesday's practice, Skattebo told Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post that the hamstring tear he sustained in a Week 7 overtime win over the Texans "wasn't too bad" and wouldn't prevent him from playing Thursday against the Commanders. With Skattebo proceeding to take every rep during Tuesday's session, he's now officially in the clear to step back into a lead role out of the New York backfield in Week 10. As a result of Skattebo's return to the lineup following a one-game absence, Devin Singletary -- who handled a season-high 23 touches in the Week 9 win over the Eagles -- is expected to see his opportunities get scaled back significantly.

13285.short: Fields caught three of five targets for 40 yards in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles.
13285.long: The rookie wideout is a distant third in the pecking order for targets behind Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely in the New York offense. For the season, Fields has 19 catches for 288 yards and one touchdown on 35 targets, averaging 36.0 yards per game across eight contests.

13833.short: Zvada made all four of his field-goal attempts and his lone PAT in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles.
13833.long: After Zvada missed both of his field-goal tries in the Giants' pre-Week 8 bye overtime win over the Texans two weeks ago, coach John Harbaugh stuck with the rookie kicker, and Zvada answered with a perfect afternoon against Philly. Zvada accounted for 13 of the team's 19 points, converting field goals from 53, 49, 38 and 49 yards. On the season, he's 17-for-22 on field-goal tries and 13-for-13 on PATs.

8131.short: Likely caught five of six targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles.
8131.long: Likely finished two targets shy of Malik Nabers' team-leading total and one receiving yard shy of Darnell Mooney's team-best mark, but the TE scored the Giants' lone touchdown of the game. That TD came on a five-yard pass in the third quarter from Jameis Winston, who replaced J.J. McCarthy (hip) for a drive and change before McCarthy returned to the game. Whether it's Winston or McCarthy under center, Likely projects to remain a key cog in the Giants' passing game for Thursday's Week 10 matchup against the Commanders, whose defense Likely carved up for 11 catches, 94 yards and two TDs in their Week 5 tie.

6130.short: Singletary rushed 21 times for 31 yards and caught two of three targets for eight yards in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles.
6130.long: Singletary blew by his previous season high of six carries, as fellow running backs Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy were both sidelined by hamstring injuries. Skattebo has a chance to return for Thursday's Week 10 matchup against the Commanders, while Tracy won't be back prior to Week 12, so Singletary is likely to maintain an elevated role unless the Giants trade for another running back prior to Tuesday's deadline. Singletary didn't make the most of his added opportunities against the Eagles, averaging a meager 1.5 yards per carry.

11632.short: Nabers caught five of eight targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles.
11632.long: Nabers recorded at least 111 receiving yards in four consecutive games prior to the Giants' Week 8 bye but failed to extend that streak in Sunday's low-scoring win, during which J.J. McCarthy (hip) and Jameis Winston combined to throw for just 198 yards. The star wide receiver led the team with eight targets but finished third in receiving yards behind Darnell Mooney (54) and Isaiah Likely (53). Nabers had his hands on what would have been a 20-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter but failed to secure a diving catch attempt. McCarthy left in the third quarter but managed to return later in the second half, and he can be tentatively penciled in as the starting QB for Thursday's home game against the leaky Commanders pass defense.

9497.short: The Giants signed Hyatt from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
9497.long: Hyatt was a regular part of the wideout corps with New York during his first two NFL seasons, but his role was reduced dramatically last year, and he's spent most of 2026 on the team's practice squad. He saw his first regular-season action as a practice-squad elevation in Week 7 versus Houston and played 10 total snaps (four on offense and six on special teams) without otherwise getting into the box score. Hyatt doesn't figure to see much work on offense Sunday against Philadelphia, though he could receive a slight bump if Charlie Jones (who is questionable due to a hand injury) can't suit up.

7630.short: Newsome (concussion) wasn't listed on the Giants' injury report Wednesday.
7630.long: Newsome is healthy again after missing the Week 7 win over the Texans due to a concussion. The 26-year-old signed a three-year extension with the team Tuesday and will resume his role as one of its starting cornerbacks during Sunday's matchup against the Eagles.

7666.short: Holland (concussion) was not listed on the Giants' injury report Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
7666.long: Holland was forced to miss the team's overtime win against the Texans in Week 7 while recovering from a concussion, but he now appears to have cleared concussion protocol. The 26-year-old will be back in his starting role in New York's secondary versus Philadelphia on Sunday.

13276.short: Cooper (ankle) will be limited in Wednesday's practice, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
13276.long: Per  Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic,coach Aaron Glenn downplayed Cooper's current ankle injury, noting of the wideout, "I think he'll he just fine." Meanwhile, Connor Hughes of SNY TV relays the that Cooper's current issue is affecting the same ankle that he hurt in Week 1.

11608.short: Williams did not draw a target in Sunday's Week 9 loss to Kansas City. However, he rushed once for four yards, returned one punt for 18 yards and returned two kickoffs for 55 yards.
11608.long: Williams didn't get a ball thrown his way despite logging a 60 percent offensive snap share. While the Illinois product continues to have a role in multiple facets of the game for New York, he's not making much of an impact as a pass catcher. Williams has one or zero catches in five straight contests and has tallied only 34 receiving yards during that span.

12498.short: Taylor recorded one catch for 11 yards on two targets in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
12498.long: Even with Garrett Wilson (concussion) inactive, Taylor's two targets were his fewest in a game since Week 2, and he left that one early with a thumb injury. It was Kenyon Sadiq who had Geno Smith's eyes against Kansas City, as the rookie tight end recorded four grabs for 49 yards on four targets. Taylor is more of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option at the position.

11571.short: Davis didn't play any offensive snaps in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
11571.long: With Breece Hall back from his quad injury to form a backfield duo with Braelon Allen, Davis was relegated to RB3 duties and played 16 snaps on special teams. Davis has rushed 15 times for 44 yards, while recording five grabs for 68 yards on six targets across nine appearances this season.

6353.short: The Jets signed Reeder to their active roster Monday, Amanda Vogt of the team's official site reports.
6353.long: Reeder is returning to New York after having been released by the Jets in October. The 32-year-old has logged four tackles (one solo) across six outings this season and will likely continue to see the majority of his playing time come on special teams during his second tenure with the Jets.

10883.short: McDonald put in a request for the Jets to trade him ahead of Tuesday's deadline, Ian Rapoport and Rich Cimini of ESPN report.
10883.long: The 2023 first-round pick racked up 18.5 sacks over the previous two seasons and has three on his ledger through nine games in 2026, but he's seen his playing time tail off with the arrival of No. 2 overall pick David Bailey and the addition of Kingsley Enagbare in free agency. Though McDonald is hopeful to land with a team that can present him with a clearer path to a full-time role, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Monday that McDonald "is going to be here" once the deadline passes, per Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic.

5119.short: Sanders went 4-for-5 on field-goal tries during Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
5119.long: Sanders provided all the offense for New York in Week 9, making exactly four field goals for the second straight week and third time in the last four contests. The kicker converted attempts from 23, 48, 49 and 54 yards before pulling his lone miss wide left from 53 yards, all of which came in the first half. Sanders has now gone 21-for-24 on field-goal attempts, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far during the 2026 season.

11625.short: Mitchell failed to reel in any of his seven targets during Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
11625.long: Mitchell finished second on the team in targets behind fellow wideout Omar Cooper (11) with Garrett Wilson (concussion) unavailable. Mitchell has now gone without a reception in two of the last three contests, but he has garnered 19 targets in the last three weeks, and he figures to remain busy in Week 10 against the Bills.

13330.short: Sadiq caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
13330.long: After taking a back seat to Mason Taylor in recent weeks, Sadiq out-targeted his tight end teammate four to two against Kansas City. The rookie also closed the gap on Taylor in terms of routes, as Taylor ran 21 to Sadiq's 20 on Geno Smith's 38 dropbacks. It was easily Sadiq's most productive game since posting a 7-105-1 line in Week 3 against Detroit. He's not yet playable in most fantasy formats.

1373.short: Smith completed 18 of 32 passes for 165 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. He also rushed once for eight yards.
1373.long: Smith struggled in the absence of top wide receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion), as the Jets made four field goals in the first half before getting blanked in the second half. The veteran QB posted his second-lowest total of the season for passing yards and was held without a touchdown for the first time since Week 1. Smith could be busy in Week 10 with the 2-7 Jets likely to be forced into a pass-heavy game plan if they fall behind against the Bills.

11576.short: Allen rushed eight times for 33 yards, caught both of his targets for 21 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
11576.long: Allen was limited to 10 touches in Breece Hall's (quadriceps) return from a five-game absence, while Hall turned 18 touches into 87 yards. The 22-year-old Allen excelled during Hall's absence, topping 100 scrimmage yards in each of the previous four games, but Allen will be tough to trust moving forward in fantasy with Hall first in line for touches, especially in the negative game scripts that will likely persist for the 2-7 Jets. Allen's lost fumble was his first of the season, and he has put the ball on the ground only one other time, so at least ball security hasn't been an issue for him heading into a Week 10 home game against the Bills.

8155.short: Hall (quadriceps) rushed 15 times for 61 yards and caught three of four targets for 26 yards in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
8155.long: Hall reclaimed the lead role in his first action since Week 3, notching 87 yards on 18 touches compared to 54 yards and a lost fumble on 10 touches for Braelon Allen. The 25-year-old Hall has racked up at least 16 touches in all four of his appearances this season, and the 22-year-old Allen's four consecutive games over 100 scrimmage yards entering Sunday's action weren't enough to pry the starting role away from Hall. Expect Hall to continue leading the backfield in Week 10 against the Bills, with his superior receiving ability likely to come into play if the 2-7 Jets fall behind as expected.

13567.short: Payne (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's Week 9 clash against Kansas City.
13567.long: Payne has been on IR all season but was designated to return Wednesday. Despite being a full participant in practice all week, he isn't quite ready for game action. Payne's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 15, against Buffalo.

8395.short: Belton recorded 12 total tackles (eight solo) and a pass defensed in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.
8395.long: Belton was able to secure double-digit stops for the second time this season, finishing second on the team behind linebacker Jamien Sherwood (14). Belton is now up to 68 total tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding four passes defensed over eight contests to begin the regular season.

7841.short: Sherwood recorded 14 total tackles (five solo) during Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.
7841.long: Sherwood notched a season-high 14 takedowns in the victory, securing double-digit stops for the third time in the last five contests. The linebacker has now compiled 68 total tackles (32 solo), four passes defensed, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery over eight games to open the 2026 campaign.

13363.short: Bailey (groin) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
13363.long: After missing Week 8 with the groin injury he suffered the previous week, Bailey appears poised to return after missing just one contest. The No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 Draft, Bailey has piled up 35 tackles (21 solo), including 5.5 sacks, three forced fumbles and one pass breakup across seven starts this season.

7596.short: Moore caught one of two targets for minus-3 yards during the Eagles' 19-11 loss to the Giants on Sunday.
7596.long: Week 9 was the Eagles' first game with Joe Milton as the starter, with Tanner McKee relegated to backup duties. Milton completed 18 of his 34 passes, and his lone connection with Moore resulted in a three-yard loss. The Eagles are on a bye for Week 10, and Moore's role on the offense would evaporate if one or both of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) or Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was cleared to play in Week 11 against the Steelers on Sunday, Nov. 22.

5848.short: Brown recorded one catch for 16 yards on one target Sunday in a loss to the Giants.
5848.long: Brown logged 35 offensive snaps, well behind fellow wideouts Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper (65 snaps apiece). The Eagles were without both DeVonta Smith hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) for the third straight week, but Brown hasn't done much in their absences, tallying just five catches for 63 yards on eight targets during that span. Philadelphia is on bye for Week 10, and if Smith and/or Wicks return for Week 11 versus Pittsburgh, Brown's role figures to decrease.

13150.short: Cooper caught just two of eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
13150.long: With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) still out, Cooper played more than 90 percent of the offensive snaps for the third straight game. He's done very little with that playing time, producing five catches for 61 yards during that span. Cooper is well off the fantasy radar until he shows something in the box score, and that's if Smith and Wicks remain sidelined.

8325.short: Ebiketie will remain with the Eagles after his reported trade to the Bengals on Tuesday fell through and won't be completed, according to NFL reporter Jordan Schultz.
8325.long: Earlier Tuesday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network relayed that the Eagles agreed to send Ebiketie to the Bengals in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick. The trade wasn't cancelled due to concerns over Ebiketie's physical; instead, the Bengals opted to call it off since they would have lost a third-round compensatory pick if the deal was completed, per Rapoport. The Eagles could still look to move Ebiketie elsewhere prior to Tuesday's deadline, but barring another trade, he'll suit up for Philadelphia in its Week 10 game against Pittsburgh.

7561.short: Mitchell reverted to the Eagles' practice squad Monday.
7561.long: Mitchell has been elevated each of the past three weeks and has logged at least six touches in every game during that span. During this past Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants, he recorded six yards on three carries and caught three passes for 20 yards on four targets. The Eagles would need to sign Mitchell to the 53-man roster in order for him to be eligible to play in their next game, which will be Nov. 22 versus Pittsburgh following a Week 10 bye. That opportunity for Mitchell could depend on whether Tank Bigsby (abdomen) and/or Will Shipley (foot) return from injured reserve.

4195.short: Elliott made his lone field-goal attempt in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
4195.long: Elliott's kick was good from 45 yards, but with Joe Milton making his first start at quarterback and without DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), the Philly offense struggled to move the ball and score points. Elliott is not an exciting fantasy kicker on a tanking Eagles team.

13349.short: Stowers failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
13349.long: The rookie tight end ran just four routes on Joe Milton's 48 dropbacks against the G-Men. Grant Calcaterra ran just six, as the Eagles used more three-wide sets than multiple TE sets. Stowers would need a Dallas Goedert injury or trade to come into any fantasy value.

13294.short: Lemon caught six of nine targets for 61 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
13294.long: Lemon showed a nice rapport with QB Joe Milton in Milton's first NFL start, as the rookie first-round pick led the Eagles in catches, receiving yards and targets. Lemon has operated as Philadelphia's de facto No. 1 WR while DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) have both missed the past three games, but the Eagles could get at least one of their top two wideouts back in Week 11 against the Steelers following a Week 10 bye.

5022.short: Goedert caught five of six targets for 50 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
5022.long: Goedert finished one catch and 11 yards shy of Makai Lemon's team-leading totals in Joe Milton's first start for the Eagles. Both of Goedert's touchdowns this season came back in Week 1, and the Eagles have since changed QBs twice. Goedert's best result in the three games started by Tanner McKee was a six-catch, 61-yard outing, so the veteran TE has remained consistent even as the offense around him falls apart due to injuries. Milton, McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton are all potential candidates to start in Week 11 against the Steelers after Philadelphia's Week 10 bye.

11557.short: Milton completed 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants. He also rushed nine times for 64 yards, ran in a two-point conversion and lost a fumble.
11557.long: The big-armed Milton wasn't effective as a passer while working with a depleted receiving corps that was missing DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), but Milton showcased strong mobility and led the Eagles in rushing yards while RBs Saquon Barkley and Elijah Mitchell combined for just 28 rushing yards on 16 carries. The 2024 sixth-round pick of the Patriots played nearly the full game in the 2024 regular-season finale against the Bills and got into four games with Dallas during the 2025 campaign, but this was Milton's first regular-season NFL start. Philadelphia's Week 10 bye will provide an opportunity to evaluate a QB room consisting of Milton, the recently benched Tanner McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton. Whichever QB gets the starting nod in Week 11 against the Steelers would benefit from the potential return of Smith or Wicks after the bye.

4866.short: Barkley rushed 13 times for 22 yards and a touchdown while failing to catch his only target in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
4866.long: Barkley has mustered a meager 2.0 yards per carry over the past two games while playing through hamstring and back injuries, but he also has both of Philadelphia's touchdowns over that span, including a three-yard rushing score in the second quarter Sunday. It has been a slog offensively for the Eagles, who have tried first Tanner McKee and now Joe Milton under center since losing starting QB Jalen Hurts (IR, calf) likely for the season while also playing without top two wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). It's fair to wonder if Barkley will eventually be shut down as well to get a chance to heal as the 2-7 Eagles drop out of contention, but at least a Week 10 bye will offer him a respite before Philadelphia's Week 11 home game against the Steelers.

6815.short: Baun (back) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Giants.
6815.long: Baun exited the second half of Sunday's game with a back injury. Smael Mondon will fill in at inside linebacker opposite Jeremiah Trotter while Baun receives further medical evaluation to determine if he can return to the contest.

9230.short: McKee (ribs) is active for Sunday's game against the Giants.
9230.long: McKee has overcome his rib injury in time to suit up for Sunday's contest. The quarterback is set to back up Joe Milton against the Giants due to the absence of former starter Jalen Hurts (calf, IR).

10873.short: Smith (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Commanders.
10873.long: Smith was a full participant in Friday's practice, and he was cleared from the league's concussion protocol after passing an evaluation by an independent neurologist. His return means less defensive snaps will be available for Jalyx Hunt, Arnold Ebiketie and A.J. Epenesa.

6819.short: Pittman (foot) is making progress but won't have his practice window opened this week, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
6819.long: Pittman resumed running in late October and could resume practicing at some point in November. It won't happen this week, however, leaving the Steelers with minimal WR depth beyond DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard.

1945.short: Boswell made two of his three field-goal attempts and all three PATs in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.
1945.long: Boswell missed a 57-yard attempt on the Steelers' first offensive drive of the game. The kicker proceeded to nail 20-yard and 37-yard attempts en route to five straight made kicks. Boswell is now 18-for-23 on field-goal attempts and 16-for-16 on PATs through eight regular-season games in 2026.

13274.short: Bernard caught all five of his targets for 30 yards during Sunday's 27-6 win against Cleveland.
13274.long: Bernard led the team in catches, reeling in multiple passes for the fifth straight week and sixth time overall this year. The wide receiver has built a strong rapport with starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers, but it's unclear what Bernard's workload will look like after the Steelers have a chance to regroup and potentially acquire another pass catcher during the team's bye week in Week 9.
